title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
A system that generates deepfake pornography by placing celebrity faces onto adult video was deployed on a platform with millions of monthly visitors. The system enabled users to upload non-consensual sexual imagery of named Dutch politicians, government ministers, television presenters, athletes, and members of the Royal Family. Multiple victims filed police reports and explored legal action.

The deployment had no effective human review before content went live. Users uploading this material were advised on how to remain anonymous, and the platform appears to have operated without checking whether videos depicted real people without consent. It is not established whether the platform knew which videos contained deepfake pornography versus other content, or what steps it had taken to prevent such uploads.

What remains unclear is how many videos were created by the system versus uploaded by users, and whether the platform's operators knew deepfake pornography is illegal under revenge pornography laws in the jurisdiction where victims are located. A legislative motion was introduced to designate a government authority to remove such material, suggesting that existing mechanisms for takedown were considered inadequate.

summary:
Multiple female Dutch celebrities are considering legal action after discovering themselves in manipulated pornographic videos. These fake videos appear on an online platform that receives approximately 13 million monthly visitors. The platform hosts numerous deepfake pornography videos featuring Dutch artists, television presenters, Olympic athletes, government ministers, mayors, and members of the Royal Family. Several victims have already filed police reports or are exploring legal options, according to their managers and representatives. Interim Justice Minister Yesilgöz called the videos "sickening" and encouraged victims to report them to authorities.

Deepfake pornography involves digitally placing a celebrity's face onto an adult performer's body. Platform users who upload this material are advised to remain anonymous, likely to avoid prosecution, and earn money based on video views. Legal experts warn that without government intervention, more fake videos featuring celebrities will emerge. Deepfake content falls under revenge pornography laws and is therefore illegal. Victims can report the material to police, file mass claims, lodge complaints with the data protection authority, or contact hosting companies. Previously, television presenter Welmoed Sijtsma became a victim and later documented her experience in a documentary series, leading to a 39-year-old man's conviction and conditional sentence.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
